title: ReSim: Reliable World Simulation for Autonomous Driving

control_signal.value: Ego future trajectory (8 waypoints at 2 Hz), including hazardous non-expert ones, plus an optional high-level text command (turn left, move forward, turn right).

control_mechanism.value: Lightweight trajectory encoder (two attention blocks, linear head) feeds waypoints into the DiT input alongside video latents; command via T5 text; command dropped with p=0.5 for classifier-free guidance.

base_model.value: CogVideoX-derived 2B diffusion transformer with T5 encoder and 3D causal VAE; dynamics consistency loss, unbalanced noise sampling, three-stage training with LoRA.

datasets.value: OpenDV (1700 h front-view videos), NAVSIM, and non-expert data from the CARLA simulator for training; Waymo and nuScenes for zero-shot evaluation.

metrics.value: Trajectory Difference via inverse dynamics model, FID and FVD on nuScenes, human preference study, and NAVSIM planning scores (PDMS).

controllability_evidence.value: Waymo zero-shot Trajectory Difference (Table 1): action-free 1.13 vs Vista 5.68; expert action 0.86 vs 1.89 (GT future 0.58). Human study favors ReSim on non-expert action following.

closed_loop.value: Yes, as qualitative closed-loop visual simulation: the world model executes a driving agent's predicted action to produce the next visual state. Duration not stated; no closed-loop benchmark yet.

stated_limitations.value: Inference efficiency limited by iterative denoising; training agents inside ReSim unexplored; possible artifacts and hallucination with multiple agents; front-view only, so multi-view planners cannot be used.

notes: Also includes a Video2Reward module and planning applications beyond generation.
